features.reorderingDesc: Split video into configurable tubes, shuffle with deterministic Fisher-Yates algorithm, and restore losslessly.
features.compressionDesc: Re-encode with modern codecs (H.264/HEVC) after reordering for real file size reduction.
features.losslessDesc: Stream mode verifies preserved media content after restoration. Re-encode mode is lossy and does not claim an identical result.
features.deterministicDesc: Same seed = same shuffle. Share seed + tube map to allow anyone to restore.
features.openSourceDesc: Built with React, Node.js, TypeScript, and FFmpeg. Self-hostable with Docker.
features.localFirstDesc: No cloud upload required. All processing happens on your machine or local server.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.intro: Three simple steps to compress and restore your videos with mathematical guarantees.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Select video, set tube duration (default 1s), shuffle seed, and codec/CRF.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Video splits into keyframe-aligned tubes → shuffled → copied or re-encoded according to mode → output + tube map.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Upload compressed video + tube map → tubes restored to original order → concatenated → audio muxed → verified.

landing.keyFeaturesDesc: Built for developers and researchers who need transparent, verifiable video compression.
landing.readyDesc: Process video locally with reversible tube-based reordering. Stream mode is lossless; re-encode mode trades fidelity for size.

compress.title: Compress Video
compress.subtitle: Upload a video and choose stream copy for lossless restoration or re-encoding for smaller, lossy output.
compress.streamModeDesc: Every video and audio packet is copied untouched, so the restored file is frame-identical to the original. Reordering alone cannot shrink a file, so expect a ratio near 1.0.
compress.reencodeModeDesc: The shuffled video is re-encoded, which reduces file size. This is lossy, so restored frames will not be identical and the lossless check is expected to report a mismatch.
compress.tubeDurationHint: Target only. Tubes are cut on keyframes, so actual lengths follow the source's GOP layout.

about.title: About Reversible Compression
about.description: A tube-based video tool with deterministic reordering. Stream mode preserves encoded media for lossless restoration; re-encode mode reduces size with quality loss.
about.conceptDesc: Understanding how tube-based reversible compression works
about.tubeSegmentationDesc: Video is split into fixed-duration tubes (default 1 second) using FFmpeg's segment muxer. Splitting occurs at keyframe boundaries so each tube is independently decodable.
about.deterministicShufflingDesc: Tubes are shuffled using the Fisher-Yates algorithm with a fixed seed. The same seed always produces the same order, enabling reproducibility and shared restoration.
about.idMappingDesc: Each tube receives a unique sequential ID. A JSON tube map records the original index, shuffled index, and tube ID for each segment. This map is required for restoration.
about.reencodingCompressionDesc: After shuffling, tubes are concatenated and re-encoded with libx264 (or libx265/VP9). This is where actual compression occurs; reordering alone does not reduce file size.
about.losslessRestorationDesc: Stream mode restores packet order and verifies media content. Re-encode mode is lossy and is never described as lossless.
about.licenseDesc: Reversible Compression is open source software licensed under the MIT License. You are free to use, modify, and distribute it for any purpose.

docs.faqLosslessAnswer: Only stream mode is lossless: it copies the video and audio streams without re-encoding and verifies their content after restoration. Re-encode mode can reduce file size, but is lossy and cannot restore identical media.
docs.faqFormatsAnswer: Input: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, M4V, or WebM. Output: MP4 using the selected video codec. The tube map is always JSON.
docs.faqMaxSize: What is the maximum file size?
docs.faqMaxSizeAnswer: Video uploads default to 500MB (REVCOMP_MAX_UPLOAD_MB); tube maps default to 10MB (REVCOMP_MAX_MAP_MB).
docs.faqDurationAnswer: It depends on video length, resolution, and hardware. Typical speed is 0.5-2x realtime on modern CPUs. A 2-minute 1080p video takes about 30-60 seconds.
docs.faqDocker: Can I use this without Docker?
docs.faqDockerAnswer: Yes. Run the Node.js backend and React frontend with npm. FFmpeg and ffprobe are supplied by the backend packages; Docker Compose is also supported.
docs.faqMap: What happens if I lose the tube map?
docs.faqMapAnswer: The tube map is essential for restoration. Without it, the shuffled video cannot be restored to its original order. Always keep the tube map JSON with your compressed video.
docs.faqAudioAnswer: Yes. Stream mode copies audio unchanged. Re-encode mode encodes audio to AAC, so it is lossy along with the video.
docs.faqParallel: Can I run multiple jobs in parallel?
docs.faqParallelAnswer: Yes. The in-process backend queue accepts multiple jobs and limits active work with REVCOMP_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS (default: 1).
